messages.author: e3cd7ac95409208e
messages.subject: Random item slopes 'a' in mixedmirt() ?
parts:
Hello. I have a situation with many clusters (a little over 300)  where I suspect that both the item intercept (‘d’) and slope (‘a’) parameters differ from cluster to cluster. In order to avoid doing DIF for all these many clusters, I assumed mixedmirt() would be a great alternative, however, I can’t find any examples online where the item slopes vary randomly across groups. 

In the mixedmirt() documentation online, I only see two types of cases. Cases with  “ ~1|group” which I assume means the intercept item parameter ‘d’ is allowed to vary across groups and cases like “ 1 + covariate | group” in which a predictor effect varies across group. What would be the correct syntax to allow item parameters ‘d’ and ‘a’ to freely vary across groups? I was hoping something to find something similar to lme4 such as lmer(Y ~ 1 + X1 + (1 + X1|group)) where I know the (1 + X1|group) command will give me a random effect both for the intercept *and* the slope of X1.

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: Re: Random item slopes 'a' in mixedmirt() ?
parts:
Without authority, list(~1|group, ~1|items, ~1|group:items) might help you

Seongho

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Random item slopes 'a' in mixedmirt() ?
parts:
Currently, there is no support for random item slope parameters, only random intercept parameters. So, setting up the situation you're after is not supported yet, sorry. 

Phil

parts:
Thank you Phil & Seongho.

Do you happen to know if there is any software out there that has a "ready-made" (i.e. I wouldn't have to code it myself) routine to estimate random item slopes? STATA also only handles random intercept parameters and I'd be almost sure that Mplus can only do that as well for its multilevel SEM.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Random item slopes 'a' in mixedmirt() ?
parts:
AFAIK, the only software able to estimate those types of models are STATA with the GLAMM add on (and even then, the estimation could be extremely difficult). Otherwise, I think you'd have to use more generic MCMC software to explicitly estimate these models from a purely Bayesian perspective. 

Phil

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: Re: Random item slopes 'a' in mixedmirt() ?
parts:
I don't have any ideas what about it exists for you want to do that. 

If only can modelling random intercept per groups, that's like uniform DIF what constrained slopes as the results (because, theta = difficulty in Rasch perspectives). The random effects of the (groups:items) term, if they have variance, it may indicate evidence of weak DIF. 

In brms, 3PL multilevel IRT can make flexible (https://github.com/paul-buerkner/brms/issues/203), that is the solution to your pain.

messages.author: 6a75f6f91a59c568
messages.subject: Re: Random item slopes 'a' in mixedmirt() ?
parts:
Oh, that's the cool idea! Mplus may solve your pain, but if you want to handle 3-4PLM or assessing item fit indices, it will be hard with Mplus.

The brms::brm uses Stan as the 'engine'. The edStan ( https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/edstan/index.html ) also a good alternative for newcomer of Stan who wants to build IRT models with Stan. Stan will provide some item convergence parameters as known as PFRS or Rhat, That's very useful in modelling practice.

Good luck!

Seongho
